{"id":"ENT-1938","title":"CLI: emit outcome telemetry for entire search invocations (success, error class, result count, duration)","description":"## Why

The internal tester audit of agent transcripts (6,572 sessions across [entire.io](<http://entire.io>) / entiredb / entire-api) found that of the search sessions with no observed value, **88.5% failed to obtain a usable response at all** — 32 of 46 were auth/configuration failures, 11 were results never collected. Operational reliability, not retrieval quality, is the dominant failure mode.

We currently cannot see this class of failure in telemetry:

* `cli_command_executed` records that `entire search` ran (391 runs / 26 machines in the last 14 days) but carries no outcome, error class, result count, or duration.
* entireio/cli #2024 (`cli_commit_condensed`) answers the adoption question ("did the session search when it should have") but not "did the search work".
* These failures happen **client-side and never reach a server** — keyring/auth failures and the `ErrNoCellForJurisdiction` cell skip abort before or during the request. Server-side logging cannot catch them; the CLI is the only place they can be measured.

## What

Add outcome properties to the search invocation telemetry (extend `cli_command_executed` for the search commands, or a dedicated event if cleaner):

* `success` (bool)
* `error_class` — coarse enum, at minimum distinguishing: auth/keyring failure, jurisdiction/cell skip (`ErrNoCellForJurisdiction`), network/timeout, server error (5xx), other. Must separate the two "region" variants — the flag-gate 404 misclass (fixed in CLI v0.10.1) and the client-side cell skip are different failures.
* `result_count` (int) — zero-result searches are a distinct signal from failures.
* `duration_ms`

Covers `entire search` and `entire checkpoint search`.

## Constraints

* Content-free by construction: never send query text, result snippets, or repo names. Booleans, enums, counts, durations only (same bar as #2024).
* Gate on `ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT` and the opt-in telemetry setting before any work, matching the existing detached-child PostHog path.
* Error classes come from typed errors, not string-matching error messages.

## Explicitly out of scope

Relevance/quality telemetry (`search_id`, scores, rerank metrics, server query log) — that was PR <pull-request id="1b08f022-ffbe-4985-b38c-3d5fece15c83" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/review/add-search-id-explain-hints-and-search-relevance-telemetry-ent-1528-f1fd71e1e2cf">entireio/cli#1960</pull-request> / <issue id="804ceab6-6e3b-4dc9-9002-3a2e12696524" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1528/cli-search-click-tracking-rider-search-id-impression-log-explain-time">ENT-1528</issue>, closed deliberately. The audit shows quality was rarely the problem (4 of 52 no-value cases); revisit only after this dashboard shows the failure classes are solved.

## Done when

A PostHog query over the new properties can report, per CLI version: search failure rate broken down by error class, and the zero-result rate.","priority":{"value":2,"name":"High"},"url":"https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1938/cli-emit-outcome-telemetry-for-entire-search-invocations-success-error","gitBranchName":"evis/ent-1938-cli-emit-outcome-telemetry-for-entire-search-invocations","createdAt":"2026-08-26T04:02:36.852Z","updatedAt":"2026-08-26T04:02:36.852Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":[],"attachments":[{"id":"2890e706-c7c3-4e46-9677-8e43ece39bfe","title":"cli#1960 (closed) — search_id + relevance telemetry","subtitle":null,"url":"https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1960"},{"id":"b0323c78-3dca-49bd-bd80-8eff0b317305","title":"cli#2024 — missed-opportunity signal at checkpoint condensation","subtitle":null,"url":"https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2024"}],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"8e117581-93c5-4ca8-b53b-8fc6d2c7510f","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-08-26T04:02:36.852Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Evis Drenova","createdById":"bd1c458e-3bb3-4d0c-8ad7-e36f19afc156","team":"Entire","teamId":"832db0be-d9d8-45dc-9774-7f35babe62c0"}

---

For Entire CLI telemetry/analytics features (established during ENT-1528 search click-tracking, 2026-08-10):

- Do NOT persist tracking/correlation state under `.git/entire*` directories (or anywhere else locally). Emit stateless events and correlate later in PostHog.
- Be as privacy-conscious as possible: hash queries (never raw text), no per-result impression arrays, no derived timing fields like `seconds_since_impression` — flat, minimal event properties only.
- Goal is simple funnel visibility (e.g. which search results agents ran `explain` on), queryable later via a PostHog dashboard/MCP or Datadog — not a full client-side metrics pipeline.
- Prefer the simplest implementation that answers the product question; push complexity to the analytics layer.

**Why:** Evis rejected an impression-store design (flock'd JSON under `.git/entire/`, rank/click_seq/seconds_since_impression) as overcomplicated and insufficiently privacy-conscious.

**How to apply:** When adding CLI events, follow the existing `telemetry` package pattern (`Build*Payload` + `Track*`, settings gate at call site, `ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT`), keep properties flat and anonymous, and correlate events by `distinct_id` + time in PostHog instead of local state. See also [[plans-to-linear-tickets]].

29	// EventPayload represents the data passed to the detached subprocess.
30	// Note: APIKey and Endpoint are intentionally excluded to avoid exposing

32	type EventPayload struct {
33		Event      string         `json:"event"`
34		DistinctID string         `json:"distinct_id"`
35		Properties map[string]any `json:"properties"`

47	// BuildEventPayload constructs the event payload for tracking.
48	// Exported for testing. Returns nil if the payload cannot be built.
49	func BuildEventPayload(cmd *cobra.Command, agent string, isEntireEnabled bool, version string) *EventPayload {

53	
54		// Get machine ID for distinct_id
55		machineID, err := telemetryMachineID()
56		if err != nil {
57			return nil
58		}
59	
60		// Collect flag names (not values) for privacy
61		var flags []string
62		cmd.Flags().Visit(func(flag *pflag.Flag) {
63			flags = append(flags, flag.Name)
64		})
65	
66		selectedAgent := agent
67		if selectedAgent == "" {
68			selectedAgent = autoAgentName
69		}
70	
71		properties := map[string]any{
72			"command":         cmd.CommandPath(),
73			"agent":           selectedAgent,
74			"isEntireEnabled": isEntireEnabled,
75			"cli_version":     version,
76			"os":              runtime.GOOS,
77			"arch":            runtime.GOARCH,
78		}
79	
80		if len(flags) > 0 {
81			properties["flags"] = strings.Join(flags, ",")
82		}
83	
84		return &EventPayload{
85			Event:      "cli_command_executed",
86			DistinctID: machineID,
87			Properties: properties,
88			Timestamp:  time.Now(),
89		}
90	}
91	
92	// spawnAnalyticsHook replaces the detached spawn when non-nil so tests can
93	// assert how many sends a call performs and what each carries. Production
94	// leaves it nil. execx.SpawnDetached itself no-ops under `go test`, so counting
95	// sends needs a seam here rather than a spy on the child.
96	//
97	//nolint:gochecknoglobals // test seam, set and restored by in-package tests.
98	var spawnAnalyticsHook func(payloadJSON string)
99	
100	// spawnDetachedAnalytics sends the payload from a detached `entire
101	// __send_analytics` child so the network call never blocks the CLI. The empty
102	// dir keeps the child out of the parent's working directory. payloadJSON is
103	// one event object or an array of them — see SendEvents.
104	func spawnDetachedAnalytics(payloadJSON string) {
105		if spawnAnalyticsHook != nil {
106			spawnAnalyticsHook(payloadJSON)
107			return
108		}
109		execx.SpawnDetached("", "__send_analytics", payloadJSON)
110	}
111	
112	// maxDetachedPayloadBytes bounds the JSON handed to one child. The payload
113	// travels as an argv element and argv limits are per-platform and modest
114	// (macOS caps the whole vector near 256KB), so an oversized batch is split
115	// across children rather than risking a spawn that fails wholesale. Far above
116	// any realistic batch: one event payload runs a few hundred bytes.
117	const maxDetachedPayloadBytes = 96 * 1024
118	
119	// spawnDetachedAnalyticsBatch sends every payload using as few detached
120	// children as the size budget allows — normally exactly one.
121	//
122	// Nothing is dropped: a batch too large for one argv is split, so an unusually
123	// long backlog costs an extra process instead of lost events. Batching also
124	// means the child resolves the git version once per send rather than once per
125	// event.
126	func spawnDetachedAnalyticsBatch(payloads []*EventPayload) {
127		const (
128			bracketsBytes = 2 // "[" and "]"
129			commaBytes    = 1
130		)
131		batch := make([]json.RawMessage, 0, len(payloads))
132		size := bracketsBytes
133	
134		flush := func() {
135			if len(batch) == 0 {
136				return
137			}
138			if batchJSON, err := json.Marshal(batch); err == nil {
139				spawnDetachedAnalytics(string(batchJSON))
140			}
141			batch = batch[:0]
142			size = bracketsBytes
143		}
144	
145		for _, payload := range payloads {
146			if payload == nil {
147				continue
148			}
149			payloadJSON, err := json.Marshal(payload)
150			if err != nil {
151				continue
152			}
153			// Flush before appending so the batch stays within budget. A single
154			// payload over the budget still goes out alone: dropping it would be
155			// the silent loss this batching exists to remove.
156			if len(batch) > 0 && size+len(payloadJSON)+commaBytes > maxDetachedPayloadBytes {
157				flush()
158			}
159			batch = append(batch, payloadJSON)
160			size += len(payloadJSON) + commaBytes
161		}
162		flush()
163	}
164	
165	// IsEnvOptedOut reports whether the ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT environment
166	// opt-out is set. Every tracker honors it internally; callers that do
167	// expensive work before tracking (e.g. a git-log probe) should check it
168	// first so an opted-out user never pays for signal computation.
169	func IsEnvOptedOut() bool {
170		return os.Getenv("ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT") != ""
171	}
172	
173	// TrackCommandDetached tracks a command execution by spawning a detached subprocess.
174	// This returns immediately without blocking the CLI.
175	func TrackCommandDetached(cmd *cobra.Command, agent string, isEntireEnabled bool, version string) {
176		// Check opt-out environment variables
177		if IsEnvOptedOut() {
178			return
179		}
180	
181		if cmd == nil {
182			return
183		}
184	
185		if cmd.Hidden {
186			return
187		}
188	
189		payload := BuildEventPayload(cmd, agent, isEntireEnabled, version)
190		if payload == nil {
191			return
192		}
193	
194		if payloadJSON, err := json.Marshal(payload); err == nil {
195			spawnDetachedAnalytics(string(payloadJSON))
196		}
197	}
198	
199	// BuildPluginEventPayload deliberately omits plugin args/flags — only the
200	// allowlisted plugin name is recorded. Returns nil on failure.
201	func BuildPluginEventPayload(pluginName string, isEntireEnabled bool, version string) *EventPayload {
202		if pluginName == "" {
203			return nil
204		}
205	
206		machineID, err := telemetryMachineID()
207		if err != nil {
208			return nil
209		}
210	
211		properties := map[string]any{
212			"command":         "entire " + pluginName,
213			"plugin":          pluginName,
214			"isEntireEnabled": isEntireEnabled,
215			"cli_version":     version,
216			"os":              runtime.GOOS,
217			"arch":            runtime.GOARCH,
218		}
219	
220		return &EventPayload{
221			Event:      "cli_plugin_executed",
222			DistinctID: machineID,
223			Properties: properties,
224			Timestamp:  time.Now(),
225		}
226	}
227	
228	// TrackPluginDetached records a plugin invocation. Call sites must gate
229	// on the plugin allowlist — this function does no name filtering itself.
230	func TrackPluginDetached(pluginName string, isEntireEnabled bool, version string) {
231		if IsEnvOptedOut() {
232			return
233		}
234	
235		payload := BuildPluginEventPayload(pluginName, isEntireEnabled, version)
236		if payload == nil {
237			return
238		}
239	
240		if payloadJSON, err := json.Marshal(payload); err == nil {
241			spawnDetachedAnalytics(string(payloadJSON))
242		}
243	}
244	
245	// SkillInvocation is the content-free view of one recorded skill event: which
246	// skill fired, on which agent, and how it was detected. Deliberately no prompt
247	// text, arguments, or transcript content — and the skill name itself is only
248	// sent verbatim when allowlisted (see skillNameForTelemetry), because custom
249	// slash-command names are user content too.
250	type SkillInvocation struct {
251		// Skill is the invoked skill's name (e.g. "entire"). Names outside the
252		// official allowlist are reported as "custom".
253		Skill string
254		// Agent is the agent that surfaced the signal (e.g. "claude-code").
255		Agent string
256		// Signal is the detection signal (e.g. "prompt_slash_command",
257		// "skill_tool_use").
258		Signal string
259		// EventType is the skill event type ("prompt_invocation" or
260		// "tool_invocation").
261		EventType string
262	}
263	
264	// BuildSkillEventPayload constructs the telemetry payload for one skill
265	// invocation. Exported for testing. Returns nil if the payload cannot be built.
266	func BuildSkillEventPayload(inv SkillInvocation, isEntireEnabled bool, version string) *EventPayload {
267		if inv.Skill == "" {
268			return nil
269		}
270	
271		machineID, err := telemetryMachineID()
272		if err != nil {
273			return nil
274		}
275	
276		// Match BuildEventPayload's defaulting so the agent property is always a
277		// non-empty, queryable value.
278		agentName := inv.Agent
279		if agentName == "" {
280			agentName = autoAgentName
281		}
282	
283		properties := map[string]any{
284			"skill":           skillNameForTelemetry(inv.Skill),
285			"agent":           agentName,
286			"signal":          inv.Signal,
287			"event_type":      inv.EventType,
288			"isEntireEnabled": isEntireEnabled,
289			"cli_version":     version,
290			"os":              runtime.GOOS,
291			"arch":            runtime.GOARCH,
292		}
293	
294		return &EventPayload{
295			Event:      "cli_skill_invoked",
296			DistinctID: machineID,
297			Properties: properties,
298			Timestamp:  time.Now(),
299		}
300	}
301	
302	// TrackSkillInvocationsDetached records skill invocations, batching every
303	// event into a single detached send (split only if it would exceed
304	// maxDetachedPayloadBytes). Like TrackPluginDetached, it only honors the env
305	// opt-out itself — call sites must gate on the user's opt-in telemetry setting.
306	//
307	// No per-call cap: an earlier version truncated to 10 events, which silently
308	// dropped real invocations once condensation began extracting from transcript
309	// offset 0 — the first condensation of a session drains its whole skill-event
310	// backlog in one call, and a dropped event is never re-reported because the
311	// dedupe in session state has already recorded it.
312	func TrackSkillInvocationsDetached(invocations []SkillInvocation, isEntireEnabled bool, version string) {
313		if IsEnvOptedOut() {
314			return
315		}
316	
317		payloads := make([]*EventPayload, 0, len(invocations))
318		for _, inv := range invocations {
319			if payload := BuildSkillEventPayload(inv, isEntireEnabled, version); payload != nil {
320				payloads = append(payloads, payload)
321			}
322		}
323		spawnDetachedAnalyticsBatch(payloads)
324	}
325	
326	// CommitCondensedSignal is the content-free adoption signal emitted when a
327	// commit condenses a session checkpoint: whether the session consulted entire
328	// search, and whether the committed files already carried AI checkpoint
329	// history. Together these give the "sessions that edited history-dense files
330	// without searching" denominator that raw command counts cannot. Content-free
331	// metadata only — booleans, a count, and the agent identifier; never file
332	// paths, prompts, or transcript content.
333	//
334	// A commit is part of the event's identity, not an incidental trigger, which is
335	// why it is named for one. FilesCommitted and PriorAIHistory are commit-scoped:
336	// the former counts that commit's files, the latter asks whether commits
337	// *before* this one already touched them. UsedSearch is deliberately
338	// SESSION-scoped — the metric asks whether the session EVER consulted search
339	// before landing this commit, so one search early in a session rightly covers
340	// its later commits. The condensation paths that run without a commit (doctor
341	// repair, session-end leftovers) deliberately emit nothing — see
342	// newCommitCondensedSignal for why folding them in would corrupt the
343	// denominator rather than complete it.
344	type CommitCondensedSignal struct {
345		// Agent is the session-owning agent's registry key (e.g. "claude-code"),
346		// matching the agent property on skill and command events.
347		Agent string
348		// UsedSearch reports whether the session invoked `entire search`. Nil means
349		// the question was not answerable for this agent's transcript format, and
350		// the property is then OMITTED from the payload rather than sent as false —
351		// so a consumer filtering on `used_search = false` excludes unknowns instead
352		// of silently counting them as "did not search". UsedSearchSource always
353		// says which case this is.
354		UsedSearch *bool
355		// UsedSearchSource records how UsedSearch was determined: "unsupported",
356		// "none", "command", or "subagent". Always present.
357		UsedSearchSource string
358		// PriorAIHistory reports whether any committed file was touched by a
359		// recent AI checkpoint commit before this one. Nil means the git-log probe
360		// could not run (git unavailable, cancelled ctx, shallow-clone failure) and
361		// the property is then OMITTED from the payload rather than sent as false —
362		// same rationale as UsedSearch: a fabricated "no prior history" deflates
363		// the very miss rate this event exists to measure. A commit that landed no
364		// files is a measured false, not an omission.
365		PriorAIHistory *bool
366		// FilesCommitted is the number of files this checkpoint touched.
367		FilesCommitted int
368	}
369	
370	// BuildCommitCondensedPayload constructs the telemetry payload for one
371	// condensed checkpoint. Exported for testing. Returns nil if the payload
372	// cannot be built.
373	func BuildCommitCondensedPayload(sig CommitCondensedSignal, isEntireEnabled bool, version string) *EventPayload {
374		machineID, err := telemetryMachineID()
375		if err != nil {
376			return nil
377		}
378	
379		// Match BuildEventPayload's defaulting so the agent property is always a
380		// non-empty, queryable value.
381		agentName := sig.Agent
382		if agentName == "" {
383			agentName = autoAgentName
384		}
385	
386		properties := map[string]any{
387			"agent":              agentName,
388			"used_search_source": sig.UsedSearchSource,
389			"files_committed":    sig.FilesCommitted,
390			"isEntireEnabled":    isEntireEnabled,
391			"cli_version":        version,
392			"os":                 runtime.GOOS,
393			"arch":               runtime.GOARCH,
394		}
395		// Omitted, not false, when unmeasurable — see the doc comments on
396		// UsedSearch and PriorAIHistory.
397		if sig.UsedSearch != nil {
398			properties["used_search"] = *sig.UsedSearch
399		}
400		if sig.PriorAIHistory != nil {
401			properties["prior_ai_history"] = *sig.PriorAIHistory
402		}
403	
404		return &EventPayload{
405			Event:      "cli_commit_condensed",
406			DistinctID: machineID,
407			Properties: properties,
408			Timestamp:  time.Now(),
409		}
410	}
411	
412	// TrackCommitCondensedDetached records one condensed checkpoint's adoption
413	// signal. Like TrackPluginDetached, it only honors the env opt-out itself —
414	// call sites must gate on the user's opt-in telemetry setting.
415	func TrackCommitCondensedDetached(sig CommitCondensedSignal, isEntireEnabled bool, version string) {
416		if IsEnvOptedOut() {
417			return
418		}
419	
420		payload := BuildCommitCondensedPayload(sig, isEntireEnabled, version)
421		if payload == nil {
422			return
423		}
424	
425		if payloadJSON, err := json.Marshal(payload); err == nil {
426			spawnDetachedAnalytics(string(payloadJSON))
427		}
428	}
429	
430	// SendEvents processes one or more event payloads in the detached subprocess.
431	// This is called by the hidden __send_analytics command.
432	//
433	// The argv carries either a single event object or an array of them; both
434	// shapes are accepted. Leniency matters beyond convenience: the child is
435	// re-executed from os.Executable(), so a self-update that replaces the binary
436	// between spawn and exec can hand a payload to a build other than the one that
437	// wrote it.
438	func SendEvents(payloadJSON string) {
439		payloads := decodeEventPayloads(payloadJSON)
440		if len(payloads) == 0 {
441			return
442		}
443	
444		// Create PostHog client - no need for fast timeouts since we're detached
445		// Read API key and endpoint from package-level vars (not passed via argv for security)
446		client, err := posthog.NewWithConfig(PostHogAPIKey, posthog.Config{
447			Endpoint:     PostHogEndpoint,
448			Logger:       silentLogger{},
449			DisableGeoIP: posthog.Ptr(true),
450		})
451		if err != nil {
452			return
453		}
454		defer func() {
455			_ = client.Close()
456		}()
457	
458		// Resolve the installed git version best-effort, once for the whole batch.
459		// A missing or failing git must never block the rest of the telemetry — the
460		// property is simply omitted when it can't be determined.
461		gitVer := gitVersion(context.Background())
462	
463		for _, payload := range payloads {
464			props := posthog.NewProperties()
465			for k, v := range payload.Properties {
466				props.Set(k, v)
467			}
468			if gitVer != "" {
469				props.Set("git_version", gitVer)
470			}
471	
472			//nolint:errcheck // Best effort telemetry - don't block on result
473			_ = client.Enqueue(posthog.Capture{
474				DistinctId: payload.DistinctID,
475				Event:      payload.Event,
476				Properties: props,
477				Timestamp:  payload.Timestamp,
478			})
479		}
480	}
481	
482	// decodeEventPayloads parses the argv payload as either an array of events or a
483	// single event. Malformed input yields no payloads: telemetry is best-effort and
484	// the detached child has nowhere to report a parse failure.
485	func decodeEventPayloads(payloadJSON string) []EventPayload {
486		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(payloadJSON)
487		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "[") {
488			var batch []EventPayload
489			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(trimmed), &batch); err != nil {
490				return nil
491			}
492			return batch
493		}
494		var single EventPayload
495		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(trimmed), &single); err != nil {
496			return nil
497		}
498		return []EventPayload{single}
499	}
500	
501	// gitVersion returns the installed git version (e.g. "2.43.0"), best-effort.
502	// It returns "" when git is absent, the command fails or times out, or the
503	// output cannot be parsed — callers must treat "" as "unknown" and move on.
504	func gitVersion(ctx context.Context) string {
505		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 5*time.Second)
506		defer cancel()
507	
508		out, err := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "--version").Output()
509		if err != nil {
510			return ""
511		}
512		return parseGitVersion(string(out))
513	}
514	
515	// parseGitVersion extracts the version token from `git --version` output, which
516	// looks like "git version 2.43.0" (sometimes with a platform suffix such as
517	// "git version 2.39.3 (Apple Git-146)"). Returns "" if the shape is unexpected.
518	func parseGitVersion(out string) string {
519		fields := strings.Fields(out)
520		if len(fields) < 3 || fields[0] != "git" || fields[1] != "version" {
521			return ""
522		}
523		return fields[2]
524	}

67			Example: "  entire search \"retry backoff\" --json\n  entire search \"retry backoff\" --json --compact\n  entire search \"auth timeout author:alice date:week\"\n  entire search --code \"parseToken\"",
68			Args:    cobra.ArbitraryArgs,
69			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
70				ctx := cmd.Context()
71				query := strings.Join(args, " ")
72	
73				if caseSensitive && !codeFlag {
74					return errors.New("--case-sensitive can only be used with --code")
75				}
76	
77				if compactOutput {
78					if codeFlag {
79						return errors.New("--compact cannot be used with --code")
80					}
81					jsonOutput = true // compact is a JSON shape
82				}
83	
84				if codeFlag {
85					// Reject flags that only apply to checkpoint search.
86					for _, pair := range []struct{ flag, name string }{
87						{authorFlag, "--author"},
88						{dateFlag, "--date"},
89						{branchFlag, "--branch"},
90					} {
91						if pair.flag != "" {
92							return fmt.Errorf("%s cannot be used with --code", pair.name)
93						}
94					}
95					if cmd.Flags().Changed("page") {
96						return errors.New("--page cannot be used with --code")
97					}
98	
99					// For code search, only extract repo: inline filters from
100					// the query. Other checkpoint filters (author:, date:,
101					// branch:) are not supported and must be preserved as
102					// literal search text so "author:foo" searches for that
103					// string in code rather than being silently consumed.
104					codeQuery, inlineRepos := extractInlineRepoFilters(query)
105					codeRepos := search.AppendUnique(nil, repoFlags...)
106					codeRepos = search.AppendUnique(codeRepos, inlineRepos...)
107					// repo:* or --all-repos means "all repos" — no filter.
108					// Otherwise, if no explicit filter was given, scope to the
109					// current repo (matching the checkpoint-search default).
110					hasAllRepos := allReposFlag
111					for _, r := range codeRepos {
112						if r == search.AllReposFilter {
113							hasAllRepos = true
114						}
115					}
116					if hasAllRepos {
117						codeRepos = nil
118					} else {
119						// Remove any stray "*" entries.
120						filtered := codeRepos[:0]
121						for _, r := range codeRepos {
122							if r != search.AllReposFilter {
123								filtered = append(filtered, r)
124							}
125						}
126						codeRepos = filtered
127	
128						// No explicit repo filter → derive from git origin remote.
129						// Use forge-prefixed slug so et/ forge repos match the index.
130						if len(codeRepos) == 0 {
131							slug := currentRepoSlugWithForge(ctx)
132							if slug == "" {
133								return errors.New("could not determine current repository for code search (use --repo or --all-repos)")
134							}
135							codeRepos = []string{slug}
136						}
137					}
138					return runCodeSearch(ctx, cmd, codeSearchOpts{
139						query:         codeQuery,
140						repoFilters:   codeRepos,
141						limit:         limitFlag,
142						limitExplicit: cmd.Flags().Changed("limit"),
143						caseSensitive: caseSensitive,
144						jsonOutput:    jsonOutput,
145						insecureHTTP:  insecureHTTPAuth,
146					})
147				}
148	
149				// Extract inline filters (author:, date:, branch:, repo:) from query args.
150				// Keep the raw query for code search (which preserves author:/date:/branch:
151				// as literal text via extractInlineRepoFilters).
152				rawQuery := query
153				parsed := search.ParseSearchInput(query)
154				query = parsed.Query
155				if authorFlag == "" {
156					authorFlag = parsed.Author
157				}
158				if dateFlag == "" {
159					dateFlag = parsed.Date
160				}
161				if branchFlag == "" {
162					branchFlag = parsed.Branch
163				}
164				// Merge --repo flag values with inline repo: filters (flags first),
165				// deduped. Repeatable/comma-separated --repo mirrors code-search UX.
166				repos := search.AppendUnique(nil, repoFlags...)
167				repos = search.AppendUnique(repos, parsed.Repos...)
168				if err := search.ValidateRepoFilters(repos); err != nil {
169					return fmt.Errorf("validating repo filter: %w", err)
170				}
171	
172				// Check for repo:* in inline filters
173				allRepos := allReposFlag
174				if len(repos) == 1 && repos[0] == search.AllReposFilter {
175					allRepos = true
176				}
177	
178				w := cmd.OutOrStdout()
179				isTerminal := interactive.IsTerminalWriter(w)
180				// Mirror search.Config.HasFilters (incl. --all-repos) so an empty
181				// query with only filters isn't rejected here. This guard runs
182				// before git/auth, so it can't call searchCfg.HasFilters() directly.
183				hasFilters := authorFlag != "" || dateFlag != "" || branchFlag != "" || len(repos) > 0 || allRepos
184	
185				// Fast-fail: no query + non-interactive mode = error (before auth/git checks)
186				if query == "" && !hasFilters && (jsonOutput || !isTerminal || IsAccessibleMode()) {
187					return errors.New("query required when using --json, accessible mode, or piped output. Usage: entire search <query>")
188				}
189	
190				// Get the repo's GitHub remote URL
191				repo, err := strategy.OpenRepository(ctx)
192				if err != nil {
193					cmd.SilenceUsage = true
194					fmt.Fprintln(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), "Not a git repository. Run this command from within a git repository.")
195					return NewSilentError(err)
196				}
197				defer repo.Close()
198	
199				remote, err := repo.Remote("origin")
200				if err != nil {
201					return fmt.Errorf("could not find 'origin' remote: %w", err)
202				}
203				urls := remote.Config().URLs
204				if len(urls) == 0 {
205					return errors.New("origin remote has no URLs configured")
206				}
207	
208				owner, repoName, err := search.ParseGitHubRemote(urls[0])
209				if err != nil {
210					return fmt.Errorf("parsing remote URL: %w", err)
211				}
212	
213				// Semantic search goes to the v4 query-serve path (entire-api
214				// cell gateway) via newSemanticSearcher, which fans out across
215				// cells and mints per-cell identity tokens itself (ENT-1055).
216				searcher := newSemanticSearcher(insecureHTTPAuth)
217	
218				searchCfg := search.Config{
219					Owner:    owner,
220					Repo:     repoName,
221					Repos:    repos,
222					AllRepos: allRepos,
223					Query:    query,
224					Limit:    limitFlag,
225					Page:     pageFlag,
226					Author:   authorFlag,
227					Date:     dateFlag,
228					Branch:   branchFlag,
229				}
230	
231				// Use wildcard query when only filters are provided
232				if query == "" && searchCfg.HasFilters() {
233					searchCfg.Query = search.WildcardQuery
234				}
235	
236				// No query provided + interactive = open TUI with search bar focused
237				if query == "" && !searchCfg.HasFilters() {
238					searchCfg.Limit = search.DefaultLimit
239					styles := newStatusStyles(w)
240					model := newSearchModel(nil, "", 0, searchCfg, styles, buildCodeSearchOpts(ctx, owner, repoName, nil, false, insecureHTTPAuth))
241					model.semanticSearch = searcher
242					model.mode = modeSearch
243					model.input.Focus()
244					model.codeLoading = false // don't fetch until a query is entered
245					p := tea.NewProgram(model)
246					if _, err := p.Run(); err != nil {
247						return fmt.Errorf("TUI error: %w", err)
248					}
249					return nil
250				}
251	
252				// Fetch a full page (DefaultLimit, matching the web UI) up front and
253				// paginate client-side for all output modes; the requested --limit
254				// only controls the client-side page size.
255				requestedLimit := searchCfg.Limit
256				requestedPage := searchCfg.Page
257				searchCfg.Limit = search.DefaultLimit
258				searchCfg.Page = 0 // let API default to page 1
259	
260				resp, err := searcher(ctx, searchCfg)
261				if err != nil {
262					return fmt.Errorf("search failed: %w", err)
263				}
264				for _, warning := range resp.Warnings {
265					fmt.Fprintln(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), "warning: "+warning)
266				}
267	
268				// JSON output: explicit flag or piped/redirected stdout
269				if jsonOutput || !isTerminal {
270					if compactOutput {
271						return writeSearchCompactJSON(w, resp, requestedLimit, requestedPage)
272					}
273					return writeSearchJSON(w, resp, requestedLimit, requestedPage)
274				}
275	
276				styles := newStatusStyles(w)
277	
278				// Accessible mode: static table
279				if IsAccessibleMode() {
280					if len(resp.Results) == 0 {
281						fmt.Fprintln(w, "No results found.")
282						return nil
283					}
284					renderSearchStatic(w, resp.Results, query, resp.Total, len(resp.CountsLowerBound) > 0, styles)
285					return nil
286				}
287	
288				// Interactive TUI
289				codeOpts := buildCodeSearchOpts(ctx, owner, repoName, repos, allRepos, insecureHTTPAuth)
290				if codeOpts != nil {
291					// Use extractInlineRepoFilters on the raw query so author:/date:/branch:
292					// tokens are preserved as literal code-search text, matching --code and
293					// the TUI submit path. Inline repo: filters override the flag-based
294					// scope, consistent with TUI re-search behavior.
295					codeQuery, inlineRepos := extractInlineRepoFilters(rawQuery)
296					codeOpts.query = codeQuery // empty → no initial code search (gated in newSearchModel)
297					if len(inlineRepos) > 0 {
298						if hasAllReposFilter(inlineRepos) {
299							codeOpts.repoFilters = nil
300						} else {
301							codeOpts.repoFilters = inlineRepos
302						}
303					}
304				}
305				model := newSearchModel(resp.Results, query, resp.Total, searchCfg, styles, codeOpts)
306				model.semanticSearch = searcher
307				model.warning = strings.Join(resp.Warnings, "; ")
308				// The initial response's counts metadata must reach the model the
309				// same way a re-search's does, or the tab counts and their
310				// lower-bound "+" are missing on the first view (ENT-1777).
311				model.counts = resp.Counts
312				model.countsLowerBound = resp.CountsLowerBound
313				p := tea.NewProgram(model)
314				if _, err := p.Run(); err != nil {
315					return fmt.Errorf("TUI error: %w", err)
316				}
317				return nil
318			},
319		}

342	// completeRepoFlag returns shell-completion suggestions for the search
343	// command's --repo flag. "*" is always offered so the wildcard works
344	// regardless of auth state. Errors are swallowed (rather than surfaced via
345	// ShellCompDirectiveError) because completion runs on every TAB press and
346	// must never pollute the user's prompt with error output.
347	func completeRepoFlag(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string, _ string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
348		suggestions := []string{"*"}
349		client, err := NewAuthenticatedAPIClient(cmd.Context(), false)
350		if err != nil {
351			return suggestions, cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp
352		}
353		repos, err := client.ListRepositories(cmd.Context(), api.RepositorySortRecent)
354		if err != nil {
355			return suggestions, cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp
356		}
357		for _, r := range repos {
358			if r.CheckpointCount == 0 {
359				continue // searching a repo with no checkpoints would always be empty
360			}
361			suggestions = append(suggestions, r.FullName)
362		}
363		return suggestions, cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp
364	}

366	type codeSearchOpts struct {
367		query           string
368		repoFilters     []string
369		resolvedRepoIDs []string // ULIDs resolved from repoFilters via repo index
370		limit           int
371		limitExplicit   bool // user passed --limit; don't override for text display
372		caseSensitive   bool
373		jsonOutput      bool
374		insecureHTTP    bool
375	}
376	
377	// extractInlineRepoFilters extracts only repo: prefixed filters from a query
378	// string, returning the remaining query text and the list of repo values.
379	// Unlike search.ParseSearchInput, this does NOT consume author:, date:, or
380	// branch: tokens — those are checkpoint-search-only and should be treated as
381	// literal text in code search queries.
382	func extractInlineRepoFilters(query string) (remaining string, repos []string) {
383		var kept []string
384		for _, part := range strings.Fields(query) {
385			if strings.HasPrefix(part, "repo:") {
386				// Split comma-separated values (repo:a,b → [a, b]), matching
387				// checkpoint search's parseListFilter behavior. Trim quotes so
388				// repo:"gh/owner/repo" works like the unquoted form.
389				for _, v := range strings.Split(part[5:], ",") {
390					v = strings.Trim(v, `"'`)
391					if v != "" {
392						repos = append(repos, v)
393					}
394				}
395			} else {
396				kept = append(kept, part)
397			}
398		}
399		return strings.Join(kept, " "), repos
400	}

402	// hasAllReposFilter returns true if repos contains the wildcard "*" filter.
403	func hasAllReposFilter(repos []string) bool {
404		for _, r := range repos {
405			if r == search.AllReposFilter {
406				return true
407			}
408		}
409		return false
410	}
411	
412	// filterRepoWildcards returns repos with AllReposFilter entries removed.
413	func filterRepoWildcards(repos []string) []string {
414		var out []string
415		for _, r := range repos {
416			if r != search.AllReposFilter {
417				out = append(out, r)
418			}
419		}
420		return out
421	}

423	// buildCodeSearchOpts returns a *codeSearchOpts pre-populated with repo filters.
424	// It honors --repo, --all-repos, and inline repo: filters from the command line;
425	// when none are specified, it falls back to the current git origin slug.
426	func buildCodeSearchOpts(ctx context.Context, owner, repoName string, repos []string, allRepos, insecureHTTP bool) *codeSearchOpts {
427		var repoFilters []string
428		switch {
429		case allRepos:
430			// nil repoFilters → searchAllCells searches all repos
431		case len(repos) > 0:
432			repoFilters = repos
433		default:
434			// Use forge-prefixed slug (e.g. "et/proj/repo") so Entire forge
435			// repos match the index FullName. Falls back to owner/repo for
436			// GitHub repos (gh/ prefix is stripped by resolveRepoFilters).
437			if slug := currentRepoSlugWithForge(ctx); slug != "" {
438				repoFilters = []string{slug}
439			} else {
440				repoFilters = []string{owner + "/" + repoName}
441			}
442		}
443		return &codeSearchOpts{
444			repoFilters:  repoFilters,
445			limit:        search.DefaultLimit,
446			insecureHTTP: insecureHTTP,
447		}
448	}

450	// codeSearchCellTimeout bounds each per-cell search call (token exchange + API).
451	const codeSearchCellTimeout = 30 * time.Second
452	
453	// runCodeSearch handles the --code flag path: search code content via peregrine.
454	//
455	// When a repo filter is specified, it routes to that repo's owning cell.
456	// Without a filter, it fans out across all cells that host the user's repos
457	// (mirroring the BFF's /api/v1/stream endpoint): list repos from the control
458	// plane, group by cell/jurisdiction, search each cell in parallel, merge.
459	func runCodeSearch(ctx context.Context, cmd *cobra.Command, opts codeSearchOpts) error {
460		if opts.query == "" {
461			return errors.New("query required for code search. Usage: entire search --code <query>")
462		}
463	
464		w := cmd.OutOrStdout()
465		textOutput := !opts.jsonOutput && interactive.IsTerminalWriter(w)
466	
467		// Text output shows up to maxCodeSearchFiles files with a few matches
468		// each, so fetch a deeper result set than the default --limit (which is
469		// tuned for flat JSON output) unless the user asked for a specific limit.
470		if textOutput && !opts.limitExplicit {
471			opts.limit = codeSearchTextFetchLimit
472		}
473	
474		// Always fan out via searchAllCells — it fetches the repo index,
475		// resolves slugs to ULIDs, and handles single- vs multi-jurisdiction.
476		resp, err := searchAllCells(ctx, opts)
477		if err != nil {
478			return err
479		}
480	
481		if !textOutput {
482			return writeCodeSearchJSON(w, resp)
483		}
484	
485		writeCodeSearchText(w, resp, newStatusStyles(w), opts.caseSensitive)
486		return nil
487	}

489	// searchAllCells fans out code search across all cells that host the user's
490	// repos, using the shared cell-routing foundation (cell_fanout.go):
491	//  1. List repos from the control plane (entire-core) to discover cells
492	//  2. Resolve repo slug filters to ULIDs
493	//  3. Group by cell and resolve baseURLs via the shared helpers
494	//  4. Fan out via fanOutCells with per-cell codesearch.Search calls
495	//  5. Merge results (sorted by score, capped to limit)
496	func searchAllCells(ctx context.Context, opts codeSearchOpts) (*codesearch.SearchResponse, error) {
497		// Step 1: Get repos index from the control plane. *coreapi.Client
498		// satisfies cellCoreClient (passed to resolveCellBaseURLs below as such).
499		coreClient, err := coreapi.New()
500		if err != nil {
501			if errors.Is(err, auth.ErrNotLoggedIn) {
502				return nil, loginHintErr(err)
503			}
504			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolving control-plane client: %w", err)
505		}
506	
507		reposCtx, reposCancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)
508		defer reposCancel()
509	
510		repoIndex, err := coreClient.ListRepos(reposCtx, coreapi.ListReposParams{})
511		if err != nil {
512			return nil, fmt.Errorf("listing repos for cell discovery: %w", err)
513		}
514	
515		if repoIndex.Truncated {
516			logging.Warn(ctx, "repo index truncated; code search results may be incomplete")
517		}
518	
519		// Step 2: Resolve repo slug filters to ULIDs and narrow to matching cells.
520		indexRepos := repoIndex.Repos
521		if len(opts.repoFilters) > 0 {
522			resolved, filtered := resolveRepoFilters(opts.repoFilters, repoIndex.Repos)
523			if len(resolved) == 0 {
524				hint := ""
525				if repoIndex.Truncated {
526					hint = " (repo index was truncated — the repo may exist but was not included)"
527				}
528				return nil, fmt.Errorf("no matching repositories found for filter %q%s", opts.repoFilters, hint)
529			}
530			opts.resolvedRepoIDs = resolved
531			indexRepos = filtered
532		}
533	
534		// Step 3: Group repos by cell and resolve baseURLs via shared helpers.
535		// Routes by routedRepoPlacement like semantic search (see its doc). The
536		// CLI is deliberately ahead of the BFF's code-search.ts here, which stays
537		// canonical until its code-read chain (/symbols, /usages, file viewer)
538		// flips with it — identical behavior until then, and core electing
539		// divergent primaries is gated on that web flip (tracked on ENT-1776).
540		pinned := len(opts.repoFilters) > 0
541		cells, skippedRepos := groupReposByCell(indexRepos)
542		skippedRepos = reportableSkippedRepos(ctx, pinned, len(cells), skippedRepos)
543		if len(cells) == 0 {
544			return &codesearch.SearchResponse{SkippedRepos: skippedRepos}, nil
545		}
546		resolveCellBaseURLs(ctx, coreClient, cells)
547	
548		// Step 4: Fan out via the shared fanOutCells helper.
549		// Each cell gets the full limit for single-cell, or 2x for multi-cell so
550		// the merge sees enough candidates from every region for proper global
551		// ranking. mergeSearchResults applies the final cap.
552		perCellLimit := opts.limit
553		if len(cells) > 1 && perCellLimit > 0 {
554			perCellLimit *= 2
555		}
556		results, err := fanOutCells(ctx, opts.insecureHTTP, codeSearchCellTimeout, cells, func(ctx context.Context, group cellGroup, client *api.Client) (*codesearch.SearchResponse, error) {
557			var repoIDs []string
558			if len(opts.resolvedRepoIDs) > 0 {
559				repoIDs = group.repoIDs
560			}
561			req := codesearch.SearchRequest{
562				Query:         opts.query,
563				Repos:         repoIDs,
564				CaseSensitive: opts.caseSensitive,
565			}
566			if perCellLimit > 0 {
567				req.MaxResults = perCellLimit
568			}
569			return codesearch.Search(ctx, client, req)
570		})
571		if err != nil {
572			if errors.Is(err, auth.ErrNotLoggedIn) {
573				return nil, loginHintErr(err)
574			}
575			return nil, fmt.Errorf("code search: %w", err)
576		}
577	
578		merged, err := mergeSearchResults(ctx, opts.limit, results)
579		if err != nil {
580			return nil, err
581		}
582		merged.SkippedRepos = skippedRepos
583		return merged, nil
584	}

586	// resolveRepoFilters matches user-provided filters against the repo index,
587	// returning the ULID list for peregrine and the subset of index entries whose
588	// repos matched (for cell grouping).
589	//
590	// Matching mirrors the BFF (code-search.ts lines 315-319):
591	//
592	//	slug = filter starts with "gh/" ? strip prefix : filter unchanged
593	//	match = id === filter || full_name === slug || full_name === filter
594	//
595	// Accepted filter formats:
596	//   - ULID            — matched directly on repo ID (raw filter)
597	//   - gh/owner/repo   — GitHub repo, stripped to owner/repo for FullName match
598	//   - owner/repo      — bare slug, matched on FullName directly
599	func resolveRepoFilters(filters []string, repos []coreapi.RepoIndexEntry) (repoIDs []string, matched []coreapi.RepoIndexEntry) {
600		byName := make(map[string]coreapi.RepoIndexEntry, len(repos))
601		byID := make(map[string]coreapi.RepoIndexEntry, len(repos))
602		for _, r := range repos {
603			byName[strings.ToLower(r.FullName)] = r
604			byID[r.ID] = r
605		}
606		seen := make(map[string]bool) // dedup by ID
607		for _, f := range filters {
608			// BFF only strips gh/ prefix; other prefixes are left as-is.
609			slug := f
610			if strings.HasPrefix(f, "gh/") {
611				slug = f[3:]
612			}
613	
614			// Match order mirrors the BFF: id === filter || full_name === slug || full_name === filter
615			// FullName comparison is case-insensitive so casing differences between
616			// the git remote (e.g. entireio/CLI) and the repo index (entireio/cli)
617			// don't cause a "no matching repositories found" failure.
618			var r coreapi.RepoIndexEntry
619			var ok bool
620			if r, ok = byID[f]; !ok {
621				if r, ok = byName[strings.ToLower(slug)]; !ok {
622					r, ok = byName[strings.ToLower(f)]
623				}
624			}
625			if ok && !seen[r.ID] {
626				repoIDs = append(repoIDs, r.ID)
627				matched = append(matched, r)
628				seen[r.ID] = true
629			}
630		}
631		return repoIDs, matched
632	}

634	// mergeSearchResults merges responses from multiple cells into one, combining
635	// results, stats, and repo_stats. Results are sorted by Score (descending) for
636	// global relevance ranking and truncated to limit. Individual cell errors are
637	// logged and skipped, but if ALL cells fail the error is surfaced.
638	func mergeSearchResults(ctx context.Context, limit int, results []cellCallResult[*codesearch.SearchResponse]) (*codesearch.SearchResponse, error) {
639		merged := &codesearch.SearchResponse{}
640		var lastErr error
641		successCount := 0
642		for _, r := range results {
643			if r.err != nil {
644				lastErr = r.err
645				continue
646			}
647			if r.value == nil {
648				continue
649			}
650			successCount++
651			merged.Results = append(merged.Results, r.value.Results...)
652			merged.RepoStats = append(merged.RepoStats, r.value.RepoStats...)
653			merged.Stats.TotalMatches += r.value.Stats.TotalMatches
654			merged.Stats.TotalFiles += r.value.Stats.TotalFiles
655			merged.Stats.ReposSearched += r.value.Stats.ReposSearched
656			if r.value.Stats.DurationMs > merged.Stats.DurationMs {
657				merged.Stats.DurationMs = r.value.Stats.DurationMs // wall-clock = slowest cell
658			}
659			if merged.Query == "" {
660				merged.Query = r.value.Query
661			}
662		}
663	
664		if successCount == 0 && lastErr != nil {
665			return nil, fmt.Errorf("code search failed: %w", lastErr)
666		}
667	
668		// Track partial failures so consumers (especially --json) can see them.
669		var failedJurisdictions []string
670		for _, r := range results {
671			if r.err == nil {
672				continue
673			}
674			failedJurisdictions = append(failedJurisdictions, r.group.label())
675		}
676		if len(failedJurisdictions) > 0 {
677			logging.Warn(ctx, "code search partial failure; results may be incomplete",
678				"succeeded", successCount,
679				"total", len(results),
680				"failed_cells", failedJurisdictions)
681		}
682	
683		// Sort by score descending so results are globally ranked by relevance,
684		// not grouped by whichever cell returned first. Stable sort with a
685		// tiebreaker keeps --json output deterministic across runs.
686		sort.SliceStable(merged.Results, func(i, j int) bool {
687			a, b := merged.Results[i], merged.Results[j]
688			if a.Score != b.Score {
689				return a.Score > b.Score
690			}
691			if a.Repo != b.Repo {
692				return a.Repo < b.Repo
693			}
694			if a.Path != b.Path {
695				return a.Path < b.Path
696			}
697			return a.Line < b.Line
698		})
699	
700		// Deduplicate results that may appear from overlapping cells (e.g. a repo
701		// with empty jurisdiction searched via both home and explicit cell).
702		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(merged.Results))
703		deduped := merged.Results[:0]
704		for _, r := range merged.Results {
705			key := r.Repo + "\x00" + r.Path + "\x00" + fmt.Sprintf("%d:%d", r.Line, r.Column)
706			if seen[key] {
707				continue
708			}
709			seen[key] = true
710			deduped = append(deduped, r)
711		}
712		merged.Results = deduped
713	
714		// Deduplicate RepoStats by repo name. The fan-out routes each repo to one
715		// canonical cell (ENT-1672), so a repo appearing in more than one cell
716		// response should no longer happen via placements — this remains as a
717		// guard for overlapping cell scopes (e.g. a repo with empty jurisdiction
718		// searched via both home and explicit cell) returning the SAME content,
719		// not additional matches. Keep one representative
720		// entry per repo (the max of each count; mirror copies are identical, max
721		// only guards against minor per-cell skew) instead of summing, and record
722		// the duplicated portion so the aggregate stats can drop the double-count.
723		type repoStatAcc struct {
724			idx                    int
725			sumMatches, maxMatches int
726			sumFiles, maxFiles     int
727			cellCount              int
728		}
729		accByRepo := make(map[string]*repoStatAcc, len(merged.RepoStats))
730		var dedupedStats []codesearch.RepoStats
731		for _, rs := range merged.RepoStats {
732			acc, ok := accByRepo[rs.Repo]
733			if !ok {
734				acc = &repoStatAcc{idx: len(dedupedStats)}
735				accByRepo[rs.Repo] = acc
736				dedupedStats = append(dedupedStats, codesearch.RepoStats{Repo: rs.Repo})
737			}
738			acc.cellCount++
739			acc.sumMatches += rs.MatchCount
740			acc.sumFiles += rs.FileCount
741			acc.maxMatches = max(acc.maxMatches, rs.MatchCount)
742			acc.maxFiles = max(acc.maxFiles, rs.FileCount)
743		}
744		var overcountMatches, overcountFiles, overcountRepos int
745		for _, acc := range accByRepo {
746			dedupedStats[acc.idx].MatchCount = acc.maxMatches
747			dedupedStats[acc.idx].FileCount = acc.maxFiles
748			overcountMatches += acc.sumMatches - acc.maxMatches
749			overcountFiles += acc.sumFiles - acc.maxFiles
750			overcountRepos += acc.cellCount - 1
751		}
752		merged.RepoStats = dedupedStats
753	
754		// The per-cell Stats were summed above, so a repo answered by more than
755		// one cell was counted once per cell. Subtract the duplicated copies
756		// identified via RepoStats so the totals reflect distinct content, not
757		// the same content seen twice. This preserves per-cell truncation (the
758		// base is peregrine's own totals; we only remove the provable duplicate
759		// portion) and zero-match repos (they contribute 0 to the subtraction).
760		// A repo with matches but no RepoStats row, or a zero-match mirror repo,
761		// can't be de-duplicated from the response and keeps its summed
762		// contribution — a mild over-count, far less misleading than reporting
763		// every mirrored match twice. Clamp at zero against inconsistent input.
764		merged.Stats.TotalMatches = max(0, merged.Stats.TotalMatches-overcountMatches)
765		merged.Stats.TotalFiles = max(0, merged.Stats.TotalFiles-overcountFiles)
766		merged.Stats.ReposSearched = max(0, merged.Stats.ReposSearched-overcountRepos)
767	
768		// Cap to the caller's requested limit.
769		if limit > 0 && len(merged.Results) > limit {
770			merged.Results = merged.Results[:limit]
771		}
772	
773		// Surface partial failures in the response so JSON consumers can detect them.
774		merged.FailedJurisdictions = failedJurisdictions
775	
776		return merged, nil
777	}

809	// maxContextLineLen is the maximum number of characters to display for a
810	// context_line in grep-style text output. Lines longer than this are truncated
811	// with an ellipsis so that JSONL/minified files don't blow up the terminal.
812	const maxContextLineLen = 200
813	
814	// Text output display caps: show breadth (files) over depth (in-file matches).
815	// The fetch limit leaves headroom beyond files×matches so per-file overflow
816	// ("+ N matches") counts have data to count.
817	const (
818		maxCodeSearchFiles       = 10  // files shown in text output
819		maxCodeSearchFileMatches = 3   // matches shown per file
820		codeSearchTextFetchLimit = 100 // results fetched for text display
821	)
822	
823	// writeCodeSearchText renders code search results grouped by file (ripgrep
824	// style): a colored "repo:path" header per file, indented line-numbered
825	// matches beneath it, and a dimmed stats footer. Colors are applied only when
826	// the writer supports them (styles.colorEnabled); piped output stays plain.
827	func writeCodeSearchText(w io.Writer, resp *codesearch.SearchResponse, styles statusStyles, caseSensitive bool) {
828		if len(resp.Results) == 0 {
829			// Both causes can hold at once; reporting only the first leaves the
830			// user to discover the other from a bare result count.
831			var causes []string
832			if len(resp.FailedJurisdictions) > 0 {
833				causes = append(causes, "some regions failed: "+strings.Join(resp.FailedJurisdictions, ", "))
834			}
835			if len(resp.SkippedRepos) > 0 {
836				causes = append(causes, "skipped repos with no searchable placement: "+strings.Join(resp.SkippedRepos, ", "))
837			}
838			if len(causes) > 0 {
839				fmt.Fprintf(w, "No code search results found (%s)\n", strings.Join(causes, "; "))
840			} else {
841				fmt.Fprintln(w, "No code search results found.")
842			}
843			return
844		}
845	
846		// Group results by repo:path, preserving first-appearance order so the
847		// best-scored file stays on top (results arrive globally score-sorted).
848		type fileGroup struct {
849			key     string
850			results []codesearch.Result
851		}
852		var groups []fileGroup
853		idx := make(map[string]int, len(resp.Results))
854		for _, r := range resp.Results {
855			key := r.Repo + ":" + r.Path
856			i, ok := idx[key]
857			if !ok {
858				i = len(groups)
859				idx[key] = i
860				groups = append(groups, fileGroup{key: key})
861			}
862			groups[i].results = append(groups[i].results, r)
863		}
864	
865		shown := 0
866		for gi, g := range groups {
867			if gi == maxCodeSearchFiles {
868				break
869			}
870			fmt.Fprintln(w)
871			fmt.Fprintln(w, styles.render(styles.cyan, g.key))
872			for mi, r := range g.results {
873				if mi == maxCodeSearchFileMatches {
874					break
875				}
876				// Truncate before highlighting but append the ellipsis after,
877				// so the non-ASCII "…" doesn't disable case-insensitive
878				// highlighting (isASCII) for the rest of the line.
879				line := r.ContextLine
880				ellipsis := ""
881				if runes := []rune(line); len(runes) > maxContextLineLen {
882					line = string(runes[:maxContextLineLen])
883					ellipsis = "…"
884				}
885				lineNo := styles.render(styles.dim, fmt.Sprintf("%d:", r.Line))
886				fmt.Fprintf(w, "  %s %s%s\n", lineNo, highlightCodeMatches(line, resp.Query, styles, caseSensitive), ellipsis)
887				shown++
888			}
889			// ponytail: overflow counts only what this page fetched (peregrine
890			// has no per-file totals); a hot file shows "+ 97 matches" at most.
891			if extra := len(g.results) - maxCodeSearchFileMatches; extra > 0 {
892				label := "matches"
893				if extra == 1 {
894					label = "match"
895				}
896				fmt.Fprintln(w, styles.render(styles.dim, fmt.Sprintf("  + %d %s", extra, label)))
897			}
898		}
899	
900		var summary string
901		if resp.Stats.TotalMatches > shown {
902			summary = fmt.Sprintf("Showing %d of %d matches across %d files in %d repos (%.0fms)",
903				shown, resp.Stats.TotalMatches, resp.Stats.TotalFiles, resp.Stats.ReposSearched, resp.Stats.DurationMs)
904		} else {
905			summary = fmt.Sprintf("%d matches across %d files in %d repos (%.0fms)",
906				resp.Stats.TotalMatches, resp.Stats.TotalFiles, resp.Stats.ReposSearched, resp.Stats.DurationMs)
907		}
908		fmt.Fprintf(w, "\n%s\n", styles.render(styles.dim, summary))
909		if len(resp.FailedJurisdictions) > 0 {
910			warning := fmt.Sprintf("Warning: results may be incomplete (failed jurisdictions: %s)",
911				strings.Join(resp.FailedJurisdictions, ", "))
912			fmt.Fprintln(w, styles.render(styles.yellow, warning))
913		}
914		if len(resp.SkippedRepos) > 0 {
915			warning := "Warning: skipped repo(s) with no searchable placement (missing or not ready): " + strings.Join(resp.SkippedRepos, ", ")
916			fmt.Fprintln(w, styles.render(styles.yellow, warning))
917		}
918	}

920	// highlightCodeMatches bold-red highlights occurrences of query in line
921	// (grep convention). Matching mirrors the search: case-insensitive unless
922	// caseSensitive is set. Case folding is only applied when both strings are
923	// pure ASCII, since Unicode case mappings can change byte widths and
924	// misalign offsets against the original line; non-ASCII input falls back to
925	// exact matching. Returns line unchanged when color is disabled or there's
926	// nothing to highlight.
927	func highlightCodeMatches(line, query string, styles statusStyles, caseSensitive bool) string {
928		if !styles.colorEnabled || query == "" {
929			return line
930		}
931		haystack, needle := line, query
932		if !caseSensitive && isASCII(line) && isASCII(query) {
933			haystack, needle = strings.ToLower(line), strings.ToLower(query)
934		}
935		matchStyle := styles.red.Bold(true)
936		var b strings.Builder
937		i := 0
938		for {
939			j := strings.Index(haystack[i:], needle)
940			if j < 0 {
941				break
942			}
943			j += i
944			b.WriteString(line[i:j])
945			b.WriteString(matchStyle.Render(line[j : j+len(needle)]))
946			i = j + len(needle)
947		}
948		if i == 0 {
949			return line // no matches; skip the builder copy
950		}
951		b.WriteString(line[i:])
952		return b.String()
953	}
954	
955	// isASCII reports whether s contains only ASCII bytes.
956	func isASCII(s string) bool {
957		for i := range len(s) {
958			if s[i] >= utf8.RuneSelf {
959				return false
960			}
961		}
962		return true
963	}

965	// paginateSearchResults slices results for the requested client-side page,
966	// normalizing limit and page, and returns the page slice (never nil) plus the
967	// normalized pagination values.
968	func paginateSearchResults(results []search.Result, limit, page int) (pageResults []search.Result, total, totalPages, normLimit, normPage int) {
969		if limit <= 0 {
970			limit = resultsPerPage
971		}
972		total = len(results)
973		totalPages = (total + limit - 1) / limit
974		if totalPages < 1 {
975			totalPages = 1
976		}
977		if page < 1 {
978			page = 1
979		}
980		start := (page - 1) * limit
981		end := start + limit
982		if start < total {
983			if end > total {
984				end = total
985			}
986			pageResults = results[start:end]
987		}
988		if pageResults == nil {
989			pageResults = []search.Result{}
990		}
991		return pageResults, total, totalPages, limit, page
992	}

1035	// compactTitleMaxLen caps the title snippet length (in runes) in --compact
1036	// output so a hit never carries a full multi-KB prompt (ENT-1527).
1037	const compactTitleMaxLen = 200
1038	
1039	// compactSearchHit is the trimmed per-result shape emitted by --compact.
1040	// Field names follow the full JSON wire format's camelCase convention.
1041	type compactSearchHit struct {
1042		ID           string   `json:"id"`
1043		Type         string   `json:"type"`
1044		Repo         string   `json:"repo,omitempty"`
1045		Branch       string   `json:"branch,omitempty"`
1046		Author       string   `json:"author,omitempty"`
1047		Date         string   `json:"date,omitempty"`
1048		Title        string   `json:"title"`
1049		FilesTouched []string `json:"filesTouched,omitempty"`
1050		// CheckpointCount only appears on repo rows — without it a repo hit is
1051		// just {id, repo, title, score}, too thin for the skill's "summarize from
1052		// the compact fields alone" instruction. The repo description is not
1053		// carried: its only source was the retired MySQL repos table, so the v1
1054		// wire keeps the key but it is always null (ENT-1912, entire-search#198).
1055		CheckpointCount int     `json:"checkpointCount,omitempty"`
1056		Score           float64 `json:"score"`
1057		// Snippet is the matched text (the title is just the commit subject or
1058		// prompt head) — it's what lets an agent pick which hit to explain.
1059		Snippet   string `json:"snippet,omitempty"`
1060		MatchType string `json:"matchType,omitempty"`
1061	}

1063	// compactSnippet drops a truncated snippet that duplicates the truncated
1064	// title. When a checkpoint has no commit subject its title falls back to the
1065	// prompt, and the backend's snippet for that row is the prompt's first
1066	// indexed chunk ("Prompt: " + the same text) — the hit would carry the same
1067	// 200 runes twice (~20% of a typical compact payload). The snippet is a
1068	// duplicate when, after stripping the indexer's "Prompt: " prefix and either
1069	// side's truncation ellipsis, it is a prefix of the title; a later-chunk
1070	// snippet fails that test and is kept, since it shows where the match landed.
1071	func compactSnippet(title, snippet string) string {
1072		s := strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimPrefix(snippet, "Prompt: "), "…")
1073		t := strings.TrimSuffix(title, "…")
1074		if t != "" && strings.HasPrefix(t, s) {
1075			return ""
1076		}
1077		return snippet
1078	}

1080	// writeSearchCompactJSON writes client-side paginated search results as
1081	// compact JSON: per hit only identifiers, ranking, files touched, and a
1082	// truncated title snippet — never the full prompt. Agents fetch full detail
1083	// for a single hit via `entire checkpoint explain <id>` (add --full for the
1084	// checkpoint's entire session transcript).
1085	func writeSearchCompactJSON(w io.Writer, resp *search.Response, limit, page int) error {
1086		pageResults, total, totalPages, limit, page := paginateSearchResults(resp.Results, limit, page)
1087	
1088		hits := make([]compactSearchHit, 0, len(pageResults))
1089		for i := range pageResults {
1090			r := &pageResults[i]
1091			repo := r.ResultRepo()
1092			if org := r.ResultOrg(); org != "" && repo != "" {
1093				repo = org + "/" + repo
1094			}
1095			title := truncateOneLine(r.ResultTitle(), compactTitleMaxLen)
1096			hit := compactSearchHit{
1097				ID:              r.ResultID(),
1098				Type:            r.Type,
1099				Repo:            repo,
1100				Branch:          r.ResultBranch(),
1101				Author:          r.ResultAuthor(),
1102				Date:            r.ResultCreatedAt(),
1103				Title:           title,
1104				CheckpointCount: r.ResultCheckpointCount(),
1105				Score:           r.Meta.Score,
1106				Snippet:         compactSnippet(title, truncateOneLine(r.Meta.Snippet, compactTitleMaxLen)),
1107				MatchType:       r.Meta.MatchType,
1108			}
1109			if r.Checkpoint != nil {
1110				hit.FilesTouched = r.Checkpoint.FilesTouched
1111			}
1112			hits = append(hits, hit)
1113		}
1114	
1115		out := struct {
1116			Results    []compactSearchHit `json:"results"`
1117			Total      int                `json:"total"`
1118			Page       int                `json:"page"`
1119			TotalPages int                `json:"total_pages"`
1120			Limit      int                `json:"limit"`
1121			Counts     *search.TypeCounts `json:"counts,omitempty"`
1122			// Completeness metadata, passed through from the merged response with
1123			// the BFF's names and semantics (ENT-1777).
1124			Partial            bool            `json:"partial,omitempty"`
1125			Truncated          bool            `json:"truncated,omitempty"`
1126			CoverageIncomplete bool            `json:"coverage_incomplete,omitempty"`
1127			TruncatedTypes     map[string]bool `json:"truncated_types,omitempty"`
1128			CountsLowerBound   map[string]bool `json:"counts_lower_bound,omitempty"`
1129			Reranked           *bool           `json:"reranked,omitempty"`
1130		}{
1131			Results:            hits,
1132			Total:              total,
1133			Page:               page,
1134			TotalPages:         totalPages,
1135			Limit:              limit,
1136			Counts:             resp.Counts,
1137			Partial:            resp.Partial,
1138			Truncated:          resp.Truncated,
1139			CoverageIncomplete: resp.CoverageIncomplete,
1140			TruncatedTypes:     resp.TruncatedTypes,
1141			CountsLowerBound:   resp.CountsLowerBound,
1142			Reranked:           resp.Reranked,
1143		}
1144		data, err := jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(out, "", "  ")
1145		if err != nil {
1146			return fmt.Errorf("marshaling compact results: %w", err)
1147		}
1148		fmt.Fprint(w, string(data))

gh pr create --base main --title "feat(search): emit outcome telemetry for search invocations (ENT-1938)" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Why

The tester audit (ENT-1938) found 88.5% of no-value search sessions failed to obtain a usable response at all, dominated by client-side auth/configuration failures that never reach a server. `cli_command_executed` records that `entire search` ran but not whether it worked.

## What

New `cli_search_completed` PostHog event, emitted once per executed search request on `entire search` and `entire checkpoint search` (same command; both the checkpoint and `--code` paths):

- `success` (bool), `duration_ms`
- `result_count` — success only, so zero-result rate never counts failures
- `error_class` — from typed errors only, never message matching: `auth` (not logged in, 401/403), `cell_skip` (`auth.ErrNoCellForJurisdiction`, client-side), `region_unavailable` (`search.ErrCellUnavailable`, gateway without query-serve — kept distinct from `cell_skip` per the ticket), `repo_unavailable`, `network`, `server` (5xx), `http_other`, `other`
- plus `command`, `mode` (`checkpoint`/`code`), and the standard version/os/arch props

Plumbing needed to classify from types:

- `loginHintErr` and the all-cells-skipped path previously replaced typed causes with fresh `errors.New` — a new `hintError` wrapper keeps the user-facing message byte-identical while leaving the chain matchable with `errors.Is`.
- Semantic-search non-OK responses now return a typed `search.HTTPStatusError` (message wording unchanged); code search already returned `api.HTTPError`.

Content-free by construction: booleans, enums, counts, durations only — no query text, snippets, or repo names. Gated on the telemetry opt-in setting at the call site and `ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT` in the tracker, via the existing detached PostHog child.

## Scope choices

- Interactive TUI re-searches are not measured; the initial fetch is measured before the TUI starts, so `duration_ms` never includes TUI time. The bare-TUI entry (no query) emits nothing.
- Pre-request local failures (flag validation, not a git repo) emit nothing — the event measures search request outcomes; invocation counts stay on `cli_command_executed`.

## Validation

- New tests: payload shape (success/failure property omission), `classifySearchError` table over real error-chain shapes, `hintError` message/chain preservation, typed `HTTPStatusError` status code.
- `mise run fmt`, `mise run lint` (0 issues), `mise run test:ci` (unit + integration + canary) all pass.

Closes ENT-1938.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)"

content.text:
# Review PR

Review a pull request with structured, actionable feedback.

## Arguments

- `https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2130` — PR number, URL, or branch name. If empty, review the current branch's open PR.

## Process

### 1. Fetch PR context

```
gh pr view <pr> --json title,body,baseRefName,headRefName,additions,deletions,changedFiles,commits,author
gh pr diff <pr>
```

Read the PR description carefully — it defines scope and intent. Everything you review should be evaluated against what the PR is trying to accomplish.

### 2. Understand the change

Before reviewing line-by-line:
- What is this PR doing and why?
- What files are touched and what's the blast radius?
- Are there any architectural implications?

### 3. Review with this checklist

**Correctness**
- Does the code do what the PR description says?
- Are there logic errors, off-by-one bugs, or unhandled edge cases?
- Are error paths handled correctly?

**Security**
- Any injection risks (SQL, XSS, command injection)?
- Are secrets, tokens, or credentials handled safely?
- Are inputs validated at system boundaries?

**Testing**
- Are there tests for the new/changed behavior?
- Do tests cover edge cases, not just the happy path?
- Are test assertions meaningful (not just "doesn't throw")?

**Design**
- Does the change follow existing codebase patterns and conventions?
- Is the abstraction level appropriate (not over/under-engineered)?
- Are there unnecessary changes outside the stated scope?

**Performance**
- Any N+1 queries, unbounded loops, or missing pagination?
- Are there opportunities for batching or caching that were missed?
- Will this scale with the data sizes it will encounter?

**Readability**
- Are names clear and consistent with the codebase?
- Is complex logic adequately explained?
- Would a future reader understand the "why" behind non-obvious decisions?

### 4. Adversarial review

Take a second, adversarial pass over the diff. Actively try to break the change — assume it has flaws and hunt for them across:

- **Performance** — worst-case inputs, hot paths, allocations, contention.
- **Stability** — race conditions, partial failures, retries, resource leaks, crash recovery.
- **Correctness** — inputs and states that violate the author's assumptions.
- **Simplicity** — code that could be deleted or replaced with something simpler/stdlib.
- **Platform design standards** — deviations from the platform's established design patterns and conventions.

Add any findings to the output using the same severity format.

### 5. Run /simplify

Run the `/simplify` skill (via the Skill tool) against the changed code and fold its findings into the review output.

### 6. Structure your output

For each finding, use this format:

**[severity] file:line — short title**
Description of the issue and why it matters. Include a suggested fix when possible.

Severity levels:
- **[blocking]** — Must fix before merge. Correctness bugs, security issues, data loss risks.
- **[important]** — Should fix. Design problems, missing tests for critical paths, performance issues.
- **[nit]** — Nice to fix. Style, naming, minor improvements. Don't block merge on these.
- **[question]** — Not necessarily wrong, but needs clarification or discussion.

### 7. Summary

End with a brief summary:
- Overall assessment (approve / request changes / needs discussion)
- What the PR does well
- Top 1-3 items that need attention
- Any scope concerns (changes that seem unrelated to the stated goal)

## Guidelines

- Review what's in the diff, not what you wish was there. Don't request unrelated refactoring.
- If the PR is large, focus on the most impactful files first.
- Be specific — "this could be better" is not useful. Show what "better" looks like.
- Distinguish between "this is wrong" and "I would do this differently." Only the former is blocking.
- If you're unsure about something, use [question] severity instead of asserting it's wrong.
- Read relevant source files (not just the diff) when you need context about how changed code integrates with the rest of the system.

+package cli
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"errors"
+	"net"
+	"net/http"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/api"
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/auth"
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/search"
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/telemetry"
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/versioninfo"
+	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
+)
+
+// classifySearchError maps a search failure to a coarse telemetry error class
+// (ENT-1938). Classification uses typed errors only — never error message
+// text. Sentinel checks run before status-code checks so a mapped failure
+// (e.g. the gateway 404 behind search.ErrCellUnavailable) keeps its specific
+// class.
+func classifySearchError(err error) string {
+	switch {
+	case errors.Is(err, auth.ErrNotLoggedIn):
+		return telemetry.SearchErrClassAuth
+	case errors.Is(err, auth.ErrNoCellForJurisdiction):
+		return telemetry.SearchErrClassCellSkip
+	case errors.Is(err, search.ErrCellUnavailable), errors.Is(err, errNoRegionAvailable):
+		return telemetry.SearchErrClassRegionUnavailable
+	case errors.Is(err, search.ErrRepoFilterUnmatched), errors.Is(err, errNoRepoAvailable):
+		return telemetry.SearchErrClassRepoUnavailable
+	}
+
+	var statusErr *search.HTTPStatusError
+	if errors.As(err, &statusErr) {
+		return classForHTTPStatus(statusErr.StatusCode)
+	}
+	var httpErr *api.HTTPError
+	if errors.As(err, &httpErr) {
+		return classForHTTPStatus(httpErr.StatusCode)
+	}
+
+	var netErr net.Error
+	if errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) || errors.As(err, &netErr) {
+		return telemetry.SearchErrClassNetwork
+	}
+
+	return telemetry.SearchErrClassOther
+}
+
+func classForHTTPStatus(status int) string {
+	switch {
+	case status >= http.StatusInternalServerError:
+		return telemetry.SearchErrClassServer
+	case status == http.StatusUnauthorized || status == http.StatusForbidden:
+		return telemetry.SearchErrClassAuth
+	default:
+		return telemetry.SearchErrClassHTTPOther
+	}
+}
+
+// emitSearchOutcome reports one search request's outcome when telemetry is
+// opted in (settings.Telemetry == true). Content-free: booleans, enums,
+// counts, and durations only — never query text, results, or repo names.
+// Best-effort and non-blocking; failures to load settings suppress the event.
+func emitSearchOutcome(ctx context.Context, cmd *cobra.Command, mode string, resultCount int, duration time.Duration, err error) {
+	s, loadErr := LoadEntireSettings(ctx)
+	if loadErr != nil || !s.IsTelemetryEnabled() {
+		return
+	}
+
+	outcome := telemetry.SearchOutcome{
+		Command:    cmd.CommandPath(),
+		Mode:       mode,
+		Success:    err == nil,
+		DurationMS: duration.Milliseconds(),
+	}
+	if err != nil {
+		outcome.ErrorClass = classifySearchError(err)
+	} else {
+		outcome.ResultCount = resultCount
+	}
+	telemetry.TrackSearchOutcomeDetached(outcome, s.Enabled, versioninfo.Version)
+}

+package telemetry
+
+import (
+	"encoding/json"
+	"runtime"
+	"time"
+)
+
+// Search modes for the cli_search_completed event.
+const (
+	SearchModeCheckpoint = "checkpoint"
+	SearchModeCode       = "code"
+)
+
+// Error classes for the cli_search_completed event. Classification is derived
+// from typed errors only (see classifySearchError in the cli package), never
+// from matching error message text.
+const (
+	// SearchErrClassAuth: not logged in, or a cell/control-plane rejected the
+	// bearer (401/403).
+	SearchErrClassAuth = "auth"
+	// SearchErrClassCellSkip: client-side skip — no entire-api cell is
+	// configured for the placement's jurisdiction (auth.ErrNoCellForJurisdiction).
+	SearchErrClassCellSkip = "cell_skip"
+	// SearchErrClassRegionUnavailable: the cell was contacted but its gateway
+	// has no query-serve route (search.ErrCellUnavailable). Distinct from
+	// SearchErrClassCellSkip — these are the two "region" failure variants.
+	SearchErrClassRegionUnavailable = "region_unavailable"
+	// SearchErrClassRepoUnavailable: cells answered but the repo is not
+	// searchable (not indexed, or not enabled for semantic search).
+	SearchErrClassRepoUnavailable = "repo_unavailable"
+	// SearchErrClassNetwork: network failure or timeout.
+	SearchErrClassNetwork = "network"
+	// SearchErrClassServer: a 5xx response.
+	SearchErrClassServer = "server"
+	// SearchErrClassHTTPOther: a non-5xx, non-auth HTTP error status.
+	SearchErrClassHTTPOther = "http_other"
+	// SearchErrClassOther: everything else.
+	SearchErrClassOther = "other"
+)
+
+// SearchOutcome carries the outcome of one search request (ENT-1938).
+// Content-free by construction: booleans, enums, counts, and durations only —
+// never query text, result snippets, or repo names.
+type SearchOutcome struct {
+	// Command is the invoked cobra command path ("entire search" or
+	// "entire checkpoint search").
+	Command string
+	// Mode is SearchModeCheckpoint or SearchModeCode.
+	Mode string
+	// Success reports whether the search returned a response.
+	Success bool
+	// ErrorClass is the coarse failure class (SearchErrClass*); empty on
+	// success and omitted from the payload.
+	ErrorClass string
+	// ResultCount is the number of results returned; only meaningful on
+	// success (zero results is a distinct signal from failure) and omitted
+	// from the payload on failure.
+	ResultCount int
+	// DurationMS is the wall-clock duration of the search request.
+	DurationMS int64
+}
+
+// BuildSearchOutcomePayload constructs the cli_search_completed payload.
+// Exported for testing. Returns nil if the machine ID cannot be resolved.
+func BuildSearchOutcomePayload(outcome SearchOutcome, isEntireEnabled bool, version string) *EventPayload {
+	machineID, err := telemetryMachineID()
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil
+	}
+
+	properties := map[string]any{
+		"command":         outcome.Command,
+		"mode":            outcome.Mode,
+		"success":         outcome.Success,
+		"duration_ms":     outcome.DurationMS,
+		"isEntireEnabled": isEntireEnabled,
+		"cli_version":     version,
+		"os":              runtime.GOOS,
+		"arch":            runtime.GOARCH,
+	}
+	if outcome.Success {
+		properties["result_count"] = outcome.ResultCount
+	} else {
+		properties["error_class"] = outcome.ErrorClass
+	}
+
+	return &EventPayload{
+		Event:      "cli_search_completed",
+		DistinctID: machineID,
+		Properties: properties,
+		Timestamp:  time.Now(),
+	}
+}
+
+// TrackSearchOutcomeDetached records one search request's outcome by spawning
+// a detached subprocess. Best-effort and non-blocking; call sites must gate on
+// the user's opt-in telemetry setting. Honors ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT like the
+// other trackers.
+func TrackSearchOutcomeDetached(outcome SearchOutcome, isEntireEnabled bool, version string) {
+	if IsEnvOptedOut() {
+		return
+	}
+
+	payload := BuildSearchOutcomePayload(outcome, isEntireEnabled, version)
+	if payload == nil {
+		return
+	}
+
+	if payloadJSON, err := json.Marshal(payload); err == nil {
+		spawnDetachedAnalytics(string(payloadJSON))
+	}
+}
